mainEntity.name: What is interior demolition and how does it differ from structural demolition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interior demolition involves the selective removal of non-structural and interior elements inside a building while keeping the exterior shell and core structure intact. Typical projects include stripping kitchens, gutting bathrooms, pulling up flooring, and removing non-load-bearing partition walls. In commercial spaces, it often refers to tenant improvement strip-outs down to the concrete slab and perimeter studs. Structural demolition, by contrast, removes foundational components, bearing walls, roof structures, or entire buildings. A selective interior demo allows property owners to reconfigure layouts, update mechanical systems, and prepare spaces for remodeling without rebuilding from the ground up.
acceptedAnswer.description: Interior demolition removes interior components like walls, floors, and fixtures while preserving the building shell. Structural demolition tears down the core framing or the entire building.
